title: Ribollita
subtitle: Tuscan bean and kale soup thickened with stale bread
excerpt: Ribollita is a thick, hearty Tuscan soup built from white beans, kale and root vegetables. Chunks of stale bread are stirred in at the end to thicken it into something closer to a stew. It improves with every reheat.
sourceNotes: Ribollita means 'reboiled' in Italian. The soup is a Florentine peasant dish that was traditionally made by reheating leftover minestrone with stale bread to stretch it further.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the bread. Thaw overnight and stir in fresh stale bread when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use your largest pot.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Even better the next day. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if it has thickened too much.

content.text: The bread is what makes ribollita ribollita. Use a good dense sourdough or country loaf that is at least a day old. Tear or cut about 200g into rough chunks and stir them in for the last 10 minutes of cooking so they absorb the broth and thicken the soup. The soup is meant to be very thick.

items.prepNote: tough stalks removed, leaves roughly chopped

content.text: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, tomato puree, rosemary, thyme and bay leaves. Cook for 2 minutes.
Tip in the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, breaking them up as you go.
Pour in the stock and bring to a boil. Add the kale, reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash roughly half the beans with a fork, then stir all the beans into the pot. Simmer for another 5 minutes.

Tear in about 200g of stale bread and stir through. Cook for 10 minutes until the bread has broken down and the soup is very thick. Remove the herb sprigs and bay leaves, taste for seasoning, and serve with a drizzle of good olive oil.

items.cause: Not enough simmering time after adding bread.
Tinned beans need a little longer in the broth.
items.fix: Cook for 10 more minutes on a gentle simmer.
